title: QuanLLM-v1.0-qm and QuanLLM CLI v0.4.0: A Domain-Adapted Language Model System for Quantum-Mechanics Learning and Problem Solving
content: We introduce QuanLLM-v1.0-qm, a domain-adapted language model for university-level quantum-mechanics learning and problem solving. It is derived from Qwen3-8B and adapted with approximately 40,000 quantum-mechanics instruction examples through low-rank parameter-efficient supervised fine-tuning. The model is delivered through QuanLLM CLI v0.4.0, our cross-platform client integrating streamed generation, provider-supplied reasoning content, multi-turn dialogue, local session persistence, symbolic computation with SymPy, and per-key token accounting. The client uses an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions interface and exposes a constrained tool surface for expression evaluation, differentiation, integration, and one-variable equation solving. QuanLLM therefore treats the model, serving interface, symbolic tools, and client experience as one technical system. The graphical summary below traces this path from the Qwen3-8B foundation model through quantum-mechanics instruction adaptation and managed serving to the CLI interaction layer. This report describes the system architecture, domain adaptation, training configuration, tool-use loop, local data handling, packaging, intended use, and operational boundaries.
